subject.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths

question: Should isolated cron jobs treat empty assistant output as silent success for all cron delivery modes, or should this PR be narrowed before merge?
rationale: The code change is small and correct at the owner boundary, but the policy changes an existing runtime failure signal into success for upgraded cron jobs.

options.title: Accept all-cron silent success
options.body: Merge this executor-boundary fix as the canonical branch and document that empty assistant output from cron means nothing to deliver, while real provider/tool failures still error.

options.title: Gate the policy before merge
options.body: Ask the contributor to narrow the flag to no-delivery jobs or another maintainer-approved boundary with matching tests.

options.title: Close in favor of another canonical branch
options.body: Pause or close this PR only if maintainers choose a different open branch and preserve this PR's proof and two-path test coverage there.

recommendation.title: Accept all-cron silent success
recommendation.body: Merge this executor-boundary fix as the canonical branch and document that empty assistant output from cron means nothing to deliver, while real provider/tool failures still error.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on the isolated cron executor handoff boundary where recent history points to this owner.
